newsitem.title: USA: CellPro loses bid to keep selling Ceprate.
newsitem.headline: CellPro loses bid to keep selling Ceprate.

text.p: CellPro Inc said Friday the National Institutes of Health denied its request to keep its Ceprate bone marrow transplant system on the market, pending its appeal of a patent infringement lawsuit.

A federal judge last week ruled against CellPro in a patent infringement lawsuit in which Baxter International Inc and Johns Hopkins University claimed rights to the technology used in the Ceprate system.
CellPro, which claimed its product could be of critical use to many cancer patients, had appealed to be on the NIH to allow it to continue selling the product pending appeal.

The CellPro Ceprate system separates stem cells from surrounding cancerous cells, improving the chances that bone marrow transplants following chemotherapy will not put the cancer back into the patient's body.
It is CellPro's only product and has been credited with saving the life of the company's president and chief executive officer, Richard Murdoch, when he was diagnosed with advanced lymphatic cancer.
"Of course we are disappointed in the NIH's decision," Murdoch said in a statement.
